mainTopic: Was משה a כהן and a king? The disputes about משה's roles, and the sources that blemished כהנים get a share of the קרבנות
overview: Earlier on the daf, רב said that משה served as a כהן. The גמרא tests this against a ברייתא that calls משה a זר regarding מרים's צרעת. רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that the job of examining נגעים is given only to אהרן and his sons. A second ברייתא about אלישבע's five joys calls משה a king. The גמרא answers that it means he was also a king. The גמרא then shows that משה's כהונה is a dispute among תנאים, with four views. This leads into side discussions: whether every חרון אף in the תורה leaves a mark, why one must respect royal authority, and עולא's claim that משה asked for kingship and was refused. The גמרא then returns to the משנה and learns from three verses of ״כל זכר״ that blemished כהנים get a share of the קרבנות. The amud ends as רב אשי begins to explain why a כהן with a temporary מום needed a special פסוק. His explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Neither משה nor אהרן could inspect מרים's mark
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: משה could not examine מרים's נגע because he was a זר, and אהרן could not because he was her relative.
steps.simpleTranslation: [משה could not have quarantined מרים, since he was a זר,] and a זר may not inspect נגעים! And if you say אהרן quarantined her, אהרן was her relative, and a relative may not inspect נגעים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is in the middle of quoting a ברייתא that it brought as a challenge to רב. The ברייתא shows that neither משה nor אהרן could have dealt with מרים's צרעת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two people are ruled out, each for a different reason. משה is ruled out because he is a זר, someone who is not a כהן. אהרן is a כהן, but he is ruled out because a relative may not judge a family member's נגע.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-כהן, someone who is not a priest
Marks of צרעת on the skin that a כהן must examine
A relative, who may not judge a family member's case
He quarantined her, closing her off for seven days to see whether the mark changes

steps.confusionAlert: The text you see starts in the middle of a sentence. The ברייתא had already said that משה could not quarantine מרים. 'And a non-priest may not inspect' is the reason it gave for that.

phrases.english: and a non-priest may not inspect the leprous marks!
And if you say Aaron quarantined her,
Aaron is a relative,
and a relative may not inspect the leprous marks!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא that was brought earlier on the daf against רב's claim that משה was a כהן.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's statement that משה served as a כהן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא assumes that משה was a זר, which goes against רב.

steps.title: ה׳ Himself handled מרים's case
steps.stepSummary: Since neither משה nor אהרן could do it, the ברייתא concludes that הקדוש ברוך הוא personally quarantined מרים, as a great honor to her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, הקדוש ברוך הוא gave מרים a great honor at that time, saying: I am a כהן, and I will quarantine her; I will declare her impure, and I will release her.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its reasoning. Because no human could handle מרים's case, ה׳ did it Himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the ברייתא's own conclusion, and it shows that the ברייתא really means משה could not act as a כהן. That is the point the גמרא will use against רב in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The Holy One, Blessed be He
I will declare her definitely impure as a מצורעת
I will release her and declare her pure

phrases.english: Rather, a great honor was given to her

phrases.aramaic: הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְמִרְיָם אוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה:
phrases.english: by the Holy One, Blessed be He, to Miriam at that time:
I am a priest, and I will quarantine her;
I will declare her impure, and I will release her.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא כָּבוֹד גָּדוֹל חָלַק לָהּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes the ברייתא after it ruled out משה and אהרן.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: ה׳ Himself quarantined and judged מרים, because no human could properly do so.

steps.title: The ברייתא calls משה a זר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points to the key line: the ברייתא clearly calls משה a זר, which contradicts רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any event, it teaches: משה was a זר, and a זר may not inspect נגעים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out exactly why it quoted this ברייתא. It says outright that משה was a זר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rest of the story is not the point. What matters is the plain statement that משה was a זר. If רב were right that משה was a כהן, the ברייתא should not have called him a זר.

keyTerms.meaning: 'In any event, it teaches': this points to the one detail in a source that the גמרא needs

phrases.english: In any event, it teaches:
Moses was a non-priest,
and a non-priest may not inspect the leprous marks!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the ברייתא quoted in steps 1 and 2 and aims it directly at רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's claim that משה was a כהן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא calls משה a זר, so he was not a כהן.

steps.title: Inspecting leprous marks is a special case
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that only for נגעים does the תורה name אהרן and his sons specifically. So משה was left out of that job, even though he was a כהן in general.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: The inspection of מראות נגעים is different, since אהרן and his sons are written in that פרשה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק defends רב. משה counted as a זר only for the specific job of examining נגעים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה gives the examination of נגעים to 'אהרן הכהן או אחד מבניו הכהנים'. Since משה is not named there, he could not examine נגעים. That is an exception for this one job. It does not mean משה was not a כהן for other things, like serving or eating קדשים.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different, meaning a special case
The shades of צרעת marks that a כהן examines
The section of the תורה that deals with a topic

steps.whyThisMatters: This answer separates two questions: whether someone is a כהן in general, and whether a specific job is given to him. That lets רב's view survive.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
The inspection of leprous marks is different,
since Aaron and his sons are written in the passage.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 13:2

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק שָׁאנֵי מַרְאוֹת נְגָעִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the source: the ברייתא's 'זר' applies only to the job of examining נגעים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Calling משה a זר means he was never a כהן at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: משה was a 'זר' only for נגעים, a job the תורה gave specifically to אהרן and his sons. He could still have been a כהן otherwise.

steps.title: אלישבע's five joys: משה is called a king
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא listing the five joys of אלישבע on the day the משכן was dedicated. It describes משה as a king, not as a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: אלישבע had five joys more than the other בנות ישראל. Her brother-in-law was a king, her husband was the כהן גדול, her son was the סגן, her grandson was the משוח מלחמה, and her brother was a נשיא שבט. Yet she was mourning her two sons.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new challenge to רב by quoting this ברייתא. It is setting up the next move: the exact objection is spelled out right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list carefully gives each relative's highest title. אהרן is called כהן גדול, but משה is called only 'king'. The challenge being built is this: if משה were a כהן, the ברייתא should have mentioned it.

keyTerms.meaning: Her brother-in-law (here, her husband's brother)
The deputy of the כהן גדול
The כהן anointed to lead the army into war
The prince who leads a tribe
A mourner (feminine)

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
Elisheva had five joys
more than the other daughters of Israel:
her brother-in-law was a king, her husband was the High Priest,
phrases.notes: The brother-in-law is משה; the husband is אהרן.

phrases.aramaic: בְּנָהּ סְגָן, בֶּן בְּנָהּ מְשׁוּחַ מִלְחָמָה,
phrases.english: her son was the deputy High Priest, her son's son was the priest anointed for war,
phrases.notes: The son is אלעזר; the grandson is פינחס.

phrases.english: and her brother was the prince of a tribe;
phrases.notes: Her brother is נחשון בן עמינדב, prince of יהודה.

phrases.english: yet she was in mourning for her two sons.
phrases.notes: Her two sons are נדב and אביהוא, who died that same day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first challenge was answered, the גמרא brings a second source against רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's claim that משה was a כהן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lists משה's title as 'king' and not 'כהן'. The full challenge comes in the next lines.

steps.title: The ברייתא calls משה only a king
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points to the key line in the ברייתא: אלישבע's brother-in-law משה was a king. That implies he was a king but not a כהן גדול, which goes against רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any event, the ברייתא teaches: her brother-in-law was a king. A king, yes. A כהן גדול, no!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא zooms in on one line of the ברייתא from the last step and uses it to challenge רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists each of אלישבע's joys by naming each relative's role. For משה it says only 'king.' If משה were also a כהן גדול, the ברייתא should have said so. So the wording suggests he was not a כהן גדול, against רב.

keyTerms.meaning: In any event, it teaches (pointing to the key line of a source)
Her brother-in-law (here: משה, the brother of her husband אהרן)
King
Yes

phrases.english: In any event, it teaches:
Her brother-in-law was a king –
phrases.notes: This means משה, the brother of אלישבע's husband אהרן.

phrases.english: A king, yes; a High Priest, no!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the challenge out of the ברייתא brought in step 5
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's view that משה was a כהן גדול
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lists each relative's role. It calls משה only a king, so it implies he was not a כהן גדול.

steps.title: Read it as: also a king
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא means משה was a king as well, in addition to being a כהן גדול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say: also a king.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rereads the ברייתא so that it no longer goes against רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא did not need to mention משה's כהונה. It added the extra point that he was also a king. Saying 'king' does not cancel his being a כהן גדול.

keyTerms.meaning: Say (read the source this way)
Also, as well

phrases.english: Say: also a king.
phrases.notes: משה was a king on top of being a כהן גדול.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'King' means only a king, not a כהן גדול
steps.terutzMaskana: 'King' means also a king, in addition to being a כהן גדול
steps.whatToRemember: רב's view survives. Calling משה a king does not rule out that he was also a כהן גדול.

steps.title: A dispute among תנאים: God's anger at the burning bush left no mark
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the question is a dispute among תנאים. It quotes רבי יהושע בן קרחה: every time the תורה mentions God's anger, it records an effect, but here no effect is recorded.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like a dispute among תנאים: 'And the anger of ה׳ burned against משה.' רבי יהושע בן קרחה says: every burning anger in the תורה has an effect stated with it, but this one has no effect stated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new section. It shows that the question of whether משה was a כהן is a dispute among תנאים, starting with רבי יהושע בן קרחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the burning bush God was angry at משה for refusing the mission. רבי יהושע בן קרחה notes that in this one case the תורה records no consequence of that anger. So by his view, nothing was taken away from משה, including כהונה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is like a dispute among תנאים
Burning anger
A mark or effect (a lasting result)

phrases.english: It is like a dispute among the tanna'im:
"And the anger of the Lord burned against Moses" –
phrases.notes: שמות 4:14

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korḥa says:
Every burning anger that is in the Torah
has an effect stated with it,
but this one has no effect stated with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רב, the גמרא shows that the question is a dispute among תנאים
steps.mimraCoreRuling: God's anger at the burning bush had no recorded effect

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן יוחי: the anger did leave a mark
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן יוחי disagrees. He says the anger did have an effect, and it is hinted in the words 'אהרן your brother the לוי.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן יוחי says: this one also has an effect stated, as it says: 'Is there not אהרן your brother the לוי?'
steps.whatsHappening: A second תנא argues that the burning bush anger did have a result. He points to a word in the פסוק as the hint.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון בן יוחי reads the same פסוק and finds the effect hidden in the word 'הלוי.' Calling אהרן a לוי seems strange, and that strangeness is where the effect lies. The next steps explain it.

keyTerms.meaning: This one too
The לוי (from the tribe of לוי)

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai says:
Even this one has an effect stated with it,
as it is stated: "Is there not Aaron your brother the Levite?" –
phrases.notes: שמות 4:14, the same פסוק as the anger.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי אוֹמֵר: אַף זֶה נֶאֱמַר בּוֹ רוֹשֶׁם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי יהושע בן קרחה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The anger at the burning bush did leave an effect, hinted in the word 'הלוי'

steps.title: Why call אהרן a לוי? He is a כהן!
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks why the פסוק calls אהרן a לוי, since he is a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't he a כהן!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises the puzzle in the פסוק that will show the effect of God's anger. It sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אהרן is famous as the כהן. Calling him just a 'לוי' seems to make him smaller. This odd wording is what needs explaining.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so that

phrases.english: But isn't he a priest!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the פסוק quoted by רבי שמעון בן יוחי
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the פסוק calls אהרן a לוי rather than a כהן

steps.title: The roles were switched: אהרן becomes כהן, משה becomes לוי
steps.stepSummary: God was telling משה: I planned for you to be the כהן and אהרן the לוי, but now אהרן will be the כהן and you will be the לוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what He is saying: I said you would be the כהן and he the לוי. Now he will be the כהן and you the לוי.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the puzzle. 'הלוי' describes אהרן's role before the change, and the change itself is the effect of God's anger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה was meant to get כהונה, but he lost it because he refused the mission. It went to אהרן. So by this view משה did not keep כהונה.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he is saying
Now

phrases.english: This is what He is saying:

phrases.aramaic: אֲנִי אָמַרְתִּי אַתָּה כֹּהֵן וְהוּא לֵוִי,
phrases.english: I said you would be the priest and he the Levite,
now he will be the priest and you the Levite.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'הלוי' hints that כהונה was moved from משה to אהרן, and that move is the effect of God's anger
steps.whyThisMatters: Here the two תנאים clearly split: for רבי שמעון בן יוחי, משה lost כהונה. For רבי יהושע בן קרחה, nothing was taken away.

steps.title: חכמים: משה was a כהן only for the seven days of the מילואים
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים take a middle view: משה served as a כהן only during the seven inauguration days.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: משה served as a כהן only for the seven days of the מילואים.
steps.whatsHappening: A third opinion in the ברייתא gives משה a temporary כהונה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה did serve during the seven days of the מילואים, when the משכן was being set up. After those days his כהונה ended. So he was a כהן, but only for a short time.

keyTerms.meaning: Served as a כהן
The seven days of inauguration of the משכן
Only

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
Moses did not serve as a priest,
except for the seven days of inauguration alone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third opinion on משה's כהונה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה was a כהן only during the seven days of the מילואים

steps.title: יש אומרים: only משה's children lost כהונה
steps.stepSummary: A last opinion says משה himself stayed a כהן, and only his descendants lost כהונה. It brings proof from two פסוקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: כהונה ended only for משה's descendants, as it says: 'And משה the man of God, his sons are named among the tribe of לוי.' And it says: 'משה and אהרן among His כהנים, and שמואל among those who call His name.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with a fourth opinion: משה kept כהונה for himself. It backs this up with פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק says that משה's sons were counted as לויים, which implies משה himself was not. The second פסוק lists משה among God's כהנים. This view fits רב, who said משה was a כהן גדול.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say
Ended, was cut off
His descendants
And it says (bringing a second פסוק)

steps.whatToRemember: There are four views on משה's כהונה. רבי יהושע בן קרחה: nothing was taken away. רבי שמעון בן יוחי: כהונה moved to אהרן. חכמים: only the seven days of the מילואים. יש אומרים: משה stayed a כהן, and only his children lost it.

phrases.english: And some say:
The priesthood ended
only for the descendants of Moses,
as it is stated: "But as for Moses the man of God,
phrases.notes: דברי הימים א 23:14

phrases.english: his sons are named among the tribe of Levi,"
phrases.notes: It says his sons were counted as לויים, which hints that משה himself stayed a כהן.

phrases.english: and it says: "Moses and Aaron among His priests,
phrases.notes: תהלים 99:6

phrases.english: and Samuel among those who call upon His name."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים: לֹא פָּסְקָה כְּהוּנָּה אֶלָּא מִזַּרְעוֹ שֶׁל מֹשֶׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A fourth opinion that disagrees with the חכמים
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה himself remained a כהן, and only his descendants lost כהונה

steps.title: Why was a second verse needed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the last opinion added 'ואומר' and brought a second פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the point of 'and it also says'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the last opinion in step 13 needed a second פסוק when it already had one. This question sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ואומר means 'and it also says.' It signals that the first proof was not fully convincing. The גמרא wants to know what weakness in the first פסוק the second one fixes.

keyTerms.meaning: And it also says: introduces an extra proof
What is / what is meant by

phrases.english: What is the point of 'and it also says'?
phrases.notes: This points back to step 13, where two פסוקים were brought. Why wasn't the first one enough?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the structure of the double proof in step 13
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the first פסוק alone did not prove that משה himself stayed a כהן

steps.title: The first verse might only be about future generations
steps.stepSummary: The first פסוק could mean only משה's descendants became לויים, so a second פסוק shows משה himself was counted among the כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you would say the first verse is written only about later generations, then it also says: 'משה and אהרן among His כהנים.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the first פסוק might only teach something about משה's children. The second פסוק, which calls משה one of the כהנים, directly proves that משה himself was a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק places משה's sons in the tribe of לוי. That fits the claim that only his descendants lost כהונה, but it does not say anything about משה himself. The second פסוק fills that gap by listing משה among the כהנים.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say: raises a possible objection
For later generations
Among His כהנים

steps.whatToRemember: According to this last opinion, משה himself stayed a כהן. Only his descendants became regular לויים.

phrases.english: And if you would say it is written only about future generations,
it also says: 'Moses and Aaron among His priests.'
phrases.notes: תהלים 99:6

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The first פסוק could refer only to descendants, so the second פסוק is needed to show משה himself was a כהן

steps.title: משה left פרעה angry, but no result is recorded
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the rule that every חרון אף in the תורה leaves a recorded mark: משה left פרעה in anger, and nothing came of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it true that every burning anger in the תורה has a recorded effect? But it is written: 'And he went out from פרעה in burning anger,' and משה did not say anything to him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the earlier rule that every time the תורה mentions burning anger, it also records what the anger caused. It challenges that rule with a case where משה was angry at פרעה and no result appears.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier claim was general: every חרון אף in the תורה has a רושם. The פסוק about משה leaving פרעה in anger seems to break this pattern, since משה did not even say anything to פרעה afterward. If one case has no result, the rule is not universal.

keyTerms.meaning: Burning anger
A mark or effect: a recorded result
But it is written! Introduces a contradicting פסוק
Not anything at all

phrases.english: And is it true that every burning anger in the Torah
has its effect stated?!
phrases.notes: This is the general rule רבי יהושע בן קרחה stated in step 8: every burning anger in the תורה has a recorded effect.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָכְתִיב: ״וַיֵּצֵא מֹשֶׁה מֵעִם פַּרְעֹה בׇּחֳרִי אָף״,
phrases.english: But isn't it written: 'And Moses went out from Pharaoh in burning anger,'
phrases.notes: שמות 11:8

phrases.english: and he did not say anything at all to him!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל חֲרוֹן אַף שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה נֶאֱמַר בּוֹ רוֹשֶׁם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the כהונה discussion and returns to the general rule about anger stated earlier in the sugya
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע בן קרחה's rule (step 8) that every חרון אף in the תורה has a recorded effect
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Counterexample: משה's anger at פרעה is mentioned, but no result is recorded

steps.title: ריש לקיש: משה slapped פרעה
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש answers that the anger did have a result: משה slapped פרעה and then left.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: He slapped him and left.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש saves the rule by explaining that משה's anger did produce an action. He slapped פרעה before walking out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to ריש לקיש, the result is hidden inside the words 'he went out in burning anger.' משה did not just leave quietly; he struck פרעה and then left. So this case also has a רושם, and the rule stands.

keyTerms.meaning: He slapped him

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
He slapped him and left.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading a hidden action into the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: משה left פרעה with no result to his anger
steps.terutzMaskana: משה's anger showed itself when he slapped פרעה, so the rule holds

steps.title: ריש לקיש elsewhere says to respect פרעה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש: in another place he says משה was told to treat פרעה respectfully as a king, so how could he say משה slapped him?
steps.simpleTranslation: Did ריש לקיש really say this? But it is written: 'And you shall stand to meet him at the river's edge,' and ריש לקיש said: He is a king, so be pleasant to him; and רבי יוחנן said: He is wicked, so be bold toward him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that ריש לקיש seems to contradict himself. In a different argument with רבי יוחנן, ריש לקיש held that משה should treat פרעה with a friendly, respectful face.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ריש לקיש believes משה was commanded to respect פרעה as a king, it is hard to say he also believes משה slapped פרעה. The challenge is internal: one statement of ריש לקיש clashes with another statement of his.

keyTerms.meaning: And did he really say? Introduces a contradiction within one person's views
Show a pleasant, friendly face
Be bold or brazen toward someone

phrases.english: And did Reish Lakish really say this?!
But isn't it written: 'And you shall stand to meet him at the river's edge,'
phrases.notes: שמות 7:15. Here הקב"ה tells משה how to meet פרעה.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: מֶלֶךְ הוּא וְהַסְבֵּיר לוֹ פָּנִים,
phrases.english: and Reish Lakish said: He is a king, so show him a pleasant face,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: רָשָׁע הוּא וְהָעֵיז פָּנֶיךָ בּוֹ!
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yochanan said: He is wicked, so be bold toward him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 17 by showing it contradicts another view of ריש לקיש
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's claim that משה slapped פרעה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Internal contradiction: elsewhere ריש לקיש says משה was told to respect פרעה as a king

steps.title: Switch the two opinions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers by reversing the names: ריש לקיש is the one who said to be bold toward פרעה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Reverse it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא solves the contradiction by switching who said what in the argument about meeting פרעה at the river. Now ריש לקיש holds that משה should be bold toward פרעה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the opinions are reversed, ריש לקיש holds that פרעה is wicked and משה may act boldly toward him. That fits well with his view that משה slapped פרעה. רבי יוחנן becomes the one who says to show פרעה a pleasant face.

keyTerms.meaning: Reverse it: switch the names of who said what

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not changing the פסוק or the two opinions themselves. It only switches which name goes with which opinion.

phrases.english: Reverse it.
phrases.notes: Switch the names: ריש לקיש says 'be bold,' and רבי יוחנן says 'show a pleasant face.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 18
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ריש לקיש said to respect פרעה, which clashes with the slap
steps.terutzMaskana: ריש לקיש actually said to be bold toward פרעה, which fits the slap

steps.title: רבי ינאי: always respect royal authority
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי teaches that one must always fear royal authority, as seen when משה spoke of פרעה's servants bowing to him but did not say this about פרעה himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ינאי said: The fear of the kingdom should always be upon you, as it is written: 'And all these servants of yours will come down to me,' but about פרעה himself he did not say this.
steps.whatsHappening: Connected to the theme of how משה treated פרעה, רבי ינאי teaches a lesson about respecting kings. משה said פרעה's servants would come and bow to him, but out of respect he did not say that פרעה himself would.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the end פרעה himself did come to משה, but משה did not say so to his face. This shows that even with a wicked king, one must keep the honor due to royal authority. רבי ינאי turns this into a general rule: always have fear of the kingdom.

keyTerms.meaning: Fear of the kingdom: respect for royal authority
Always
About him himself

steps.whatToRemember: Even when standing up to a wicked king, one must still show the respect owed to royal authority. משה did this with פרעה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This teaching sets a lasting standard for honoring government authority, even when that ruler does not deserve personal respect.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yannai said:
The fear of the kingdom should always be upon you;
as it is written: 'And all these servants of yours will come down to me',
phrases.notes: שמות 11:8, the same פסוק that describes משה leaving in anger.

phrases.english: while about him himself, he did not say it to him.
phrases.notes: משה did not tell פרעה that פרעה himself would come and bow, even though that is what really happened.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי: לְעוֹלָם תְּהֵא אֵימַת מַלְכוּת עָלֶיךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a related teaching about the respect משה showed פרעה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One must always show fear and respect toward royal authority, even toward a wicked king

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's source for honoring a king: אליהו runs before אחאב
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן brings a different פסוק to show that one must show respect to royal authority: אליהו ran in front of אחאב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says: we learn it from here: "And the hand of ה׳ was on אליהו, and he tied up his clothing and ran before אחאב."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן offers his own source for רבי ינאי's rule that one must always respect royal authority.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ינאי learned the rule from how משה spoke about פרעה. רבי יוחנן learns it from אליהו, a great נביא who still ran ahead of the wicked king אחאב to honor him. The rule stays the same; only the source changes.

keyTerms.meaning: From here, meaning this is the source
He tied up his clothing around his waist, getting ready to run
A wicked king of ישראל

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan says: from here:
"And the hand of the Lord was on Elijah,
and he girded up his loins and ran before Ahab."
phrases.notes: מלכים א 18:46

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second source for the rule רבי ינאי taught in step 20.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that one must always show respect to royal authority
steps.raayaSupportSource: מלכים א 18:46: אליהו ran before אחאב

steps.title: עולא: משה asked for kingship and was refused
steps.stepSummary: עולא teaches that משה asked to be king and was refused. He learns this from ״אַל תִּקְרַב הֲלֹם״, since the word ״הֲלֹם״ points to kingship, as with דוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא says: משה asked for kingship, but it was not given to him. The פסוק says "Do not come close הֲלֹם (here)," and ״הֲלוֹם״ always means kingship, as דוד said: "Who am I, ה׳ אלהים... that You brought me הֲלֹם."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new teaching about משה: עולא says משה wanted to be king but was told no.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the burning bush, ה׳ told משה ״אַל תִּקְרַב הֲלֹם״. עולא reads this as "do not come close to kingship," because when דוד המלך thanked ה׳ for making him king, he used the same word ״הֲלֹם״.

keyTerms.meaning: Kingship, royal rule
Literally "here" or "to this point"; עולא reads it as a hint to kingship
He asked for, requested

phrases.english: Ulla says: Moses requested kingship,
but they did not give it to him;
as it is written: "Do not draw hither,"
phrases.notes: שמות 3:5. This was said to משה at the burning bush.

phrases.english: and "hither" means nothing other than kingship,
as it is stated: "Who am I, O Lord God, [etc.]
that You have brought me hither."
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 7:18. דוד המלך is speaking about being made king.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about משה, still connected to the theme of royalty.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה asked for kingship and was refused, learned from the word ״הֲלֹם״, which means kingship.

steps.title: רבא challenges עולא: רבי ישמעאל says משה was a king
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects to עולא using the ברייתא where רבי ישמעאל calls משה, the brother-in-law of אלישבע, a king.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא raises an objection: רבי ישמעאל says, "Her brother-in-law was a king!"
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks עולא's claim that משה was not given kingship.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An earlier ברייתא said that אלישבע's brother-in-law, משה, was a king. That seems to say directly that משה did have kingship, which contradicts עולא.

keyTerms.meaning: Her brother-in-law (her husband's brother)

phrases.english: Rava raises an objection:
Rabbi Yishmael says: her brother-in-law was a king!
phrases.notes: This is from the ברייתא quoted earlier about אלישבע. She married אהרן, so her brother-in-law is משה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges עולא's statement in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's claim that משה was not given kingship
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא openly calls משה a king, so he must have received kingship.

steps.title: רבא: משה was refused kingship for his descendants
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that עולא meant משה was not given a kingship that would pass to his children. He himself was a king.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: עולא is talking about kingship for him and for his children.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains עולא's statement so that it fits with רבי ישמעאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה did rule as king during his own lifetime, as רבי ישמעאל said. What he asked for and was denied was a kingship that would continue in his family, so ״הֲלֹם״ hints at a kingship that lasts for generations.

keyTerms.meaning: For him and his descendants
He is saying, he means

steps.confusionAlert: Both the challenge and the answer here come from רבא. He raises the problem himself and then solves it.

phrases.english: Rava said:
He is saying for him and for his descendants.
phrases.notes: עולא only said משה was denied a kingship his children would inherit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows the scope of the original statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: עולא meant משה had no kingship at all, which contradicts רבי ישמעאל.
steps.terutzMaskana: משה was a king himself; he was refused only a kingship that passes to his descendants.

steps.title: Challenge: שאול was called ״הֲלֹם״ but his children did not rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether ״הֲלוֹם״ really always means kingship for generations. With שאול, the word ״הֲלֹם״ is used, yet only he ruled and his children did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does ״הֲלוֹם״ always mean kingship for generations? About שאול it is written "Is there yet a man who comes הֲלֹם", and he was king but his children were not!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's answer, which assumed that ״הֲלוֹם״ means a kingship that passes to one's children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's answer depends on reading ״הֲלוֹם״ as kingship for future generations. The פסוק about שאול uses ״הֲלֹם״, but שאול's kingship did not pass to his children. So ״הֲלוֹם״ cannot automatically mean kingship for generations.

keyTerms.meaning: For future generations
He yes, his descendants no
The first king of ישראל, whose children did not inherit the throne

phrases.english: And anywhere that "hither" is written,
is it for generations?!
But isn't it written about Saul:
"Is there yet a man who comes hither"
phrases.notes: שמואל א 10:22

phrases.english: he, yes; his descendants, no!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading of ״הֲלוֹם״ that רבא's answer in step 24 relies on.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's reading that ״הֲלוֹם״ means kingship for future generations
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ״הֲלֹם״ is used for שאול, whose kingship did not pass to his children. So the word cannot always mean kingship for generations.

steps.title: First answer: שאול's son איש בשת did become king
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the question from שאול by pointing out that his son איש בשת did rule, so the kingship did pass on.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, you can say: there was איש בשת, who was king after שאול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 25. It says שאול's kingship actually did pass to his son איש בשת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed that only שאול ruled and none of his children did. This answer rejects that assumption, because איש בשת, שאול's son, also ruled. So the rule that ״הלם״ means kingship for generations still holds.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say: introduces one of several possible answers
שאול's son, who ruled as king after him

phrases.english: If you wish, say:
there was איש בשת,
phrases.notes: איש בשת was שאול's son, and he was king after him, so the kingship did pass on.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: הָא הֲוָה אִישׁ בּשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from שאול raised in Step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the factual assumption behind the question
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שאול's kingship ended with him, so ״הלם״ did not bring kingship for generations.
steps.terutzMaskana: שאול's son איש בשת did rule, so the kingship did pass on.

steps.title: Second answer: שאול is different because he lost the kingship himself
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: שאול is a special case, because his kingship did not last even for himself, so naturally it did not pass to his children.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you want, say: שאול is different, because the kingship did not even stay with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different answer to the question from שאול. His case is an exception, because he lost the kingship in his own lifetime.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer agrees that שאול's children did not keep the kingship. It explains that this happened only because שאול himself lost it. The rule that ״הלם״ means kingship for generations still stands, and שאול's case is an unusual outcome, not a disproof of it.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different: the case is an exception
In himself, in his own lifetime
It did not stand, it did not last

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
שאול is different,
for even in himself it did not stand;
phrases.notes: He means the kingship did not stay with שאול even for his own whole life.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, separate answer to the same question from Step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Treats the case as an exception
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שאול's case shows that ״הלם״ does not mean kingship for generations.
steps.terutzMaskana: שאול lost the kingship himself, so his case does not count against the rule.

steps.title: Support: greatness lasts for generations unless a person becomes arrogant
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר in the name of רבי חנינא teaches that greatness given from Heaven is meant for a person and his children forever, but if he becomes arrogant, הקדוש ברוך הוא lowers him.
steps.simpleTranslation: This follows what רבי אלעזר said in the name of רבי חנינא. When greatness is given to a person, it is given to him and his children until the end of all generations, as it says: ״He does not take His eyes off the righteous, and with kings on the throne…״. But if he becomes arrogant, הקדוש ברוך הוא brings him down, as it says: ״And if they are bound in chains, caught in cords of affliction״.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the second answer with a teaching of רבי אלעזר in the name of רבי חנינא. Greatness is meant to last for generations, but arrogance can make a person lose it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This teaching explains how both things can be true. Kingship is normally given for generations, as the rule about ״הלם״ says. Arrogance is a reason Heaven can take it away, and that is why שאול's kingship ended.

keyTerms.meaning: Greatness is decreed, it is assigned from Heaven
To him and to his descendants
He became arrogant
He lowers him, he humbles him

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers about שאול. Either his son איש בשת did rule, or שאול is an exception because he lost the kingship himself. רבי חנינא explains that greatness lasts for generations unless a person becomes arrogant.
steps.whyThisMatters: It closes the kingship discussion and keeps the rule that ״הלם״ means kingship for generations.

phrases.english: As רבי אלעזר said in the name of רבי חנינא:
When greatness is decreed for a person,
it is decreed for him and for his descendants
until the end of all generations,
as it says: "He does not withdraw His eyes from the righteous,
phrases.notes: איוב 36:7

phrases.english: and with kings on the throne, etc."
But if he became arrogant,
the Holy One, Blessed be He, lowers him,
as it says: "And if they are bound in chains,
phrases.notes: איוב 36:8, the very next פסוק.

phrases.english: caught in cords of affliction."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the second answer given in Step 27.
steps.raayaObject: That שאול's case is an exception, because a person can lose greatness that was meant for generations.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אלעזר in the name of רבי חנינא, based on איוב 36:7-8.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: where do we learn the law of בעלי מומין?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה about כהנים with blemishes and asks for the source of the law.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: "בעלי מומין, whether they have a temporary blemish or a permanent one…" Where do we learn this?
steps.whatsHappening: The kingship side topic is over, and the גמרא goes back to the משנה. This step sets up the next move by asking for the source that בעלי מומין share in the קרבנות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה taught that כהנים with blemishes, whether temporary or permanent, get a share and eat but do not do the service. The גמרא now wants to know which פסוק this comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: כהנים who have a physical blemish
From where do we know these words? A request for the source

steps.confusionAlert: This is a new topic. The kingship discussion is finished, and we are back to the laws of the משנה.

phrases.aramaic: בַּעֲלֵי מוּמִין, בֵּין בַּעֲלֵי מוּמִין כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: Blemished כהנים, whether blemished, etc.
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה. Blemished כהנים, with a temporary or a permanent blemish, get a share and eat, but they do not offer.

phrases.english: From where are these words?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the kingship discussion and returns to the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source that blemished כהנים receive a share of the קרבנות.

steps.title: ״כל זכר״ includes בעלי מומין
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the words ״כל זכר״ that blemished כהנים are included.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the רבנן taught: "Every male" comes to include blemished כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. The words ״כל זכר״ come to include blemished כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ״כל״ (every) widens the group. It teaches that even כהנים with a blemish are part of "every male" among the sons of אהרן. The ברייתא does not yet say what they are included in.

keyTerms.meaning: Every male (ויקרא 6:11)
To include

phrases.english: As the רבנן taught:
"Every male" comes to include blemished כהנים.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:11

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתָנוּ רַבָּנַן: כׇּל זָכָר לְרַבּוֹת בַּעֲלֵי מוּמִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 29.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra word in ״כל זכר״ includes blemished כהנים.

steps.title: Included for what? Eating is already taught elsewhere
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what ״כל זכר״ includes them in. It cannot be eating, since another פסוק already allows a blemished כהן to eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what is it needed? If it is to let them eat, it already says: "The bread of his God, from the holiest of holies, he may eat"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what exactly ״כל זכר״ includes blemished כהנים in. It shows the answer cannot be eating, because a different פסוק already teaches that. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פסוק is not needed to teach something the תורה already says. ויקרא 21:22 already states that a blemished כהן may eat קדשי קדשים. So ״כל זכר״ must be teaching something else.

keyTerms.meaning: For what? What is this needed for?
Eating the קרבנות
It has already been stated

phrases.english: For what?
phrases.notes: In other words, what exactly does ״כל זכר״ include them in?

phrases.english: If for eating,
it has already been stated:
"The bread of his God, from the most holy, he may eat"!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:22, said about a כהן who has a blemish.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַאי? אִי לַאֲכִילָה הֲרֵי כְּבָר נֶאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions what the ברייתא's derivation in Step 30 is needed for.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What ״כל זכר״ includes blemished כהנים in, given that eating is already taught.

steps.title: It teaches that they get a share in the dividing
steps.stepSummary: ״כל זכר״ teaches that blemished כהנים get a share when the קרבנות are divided.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is needed for the dividing of shares.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that ״כל זכר״ teaches that blemished כהנים get a share when the קרבנות are divided up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being allowed to eat and getting a share in the division are two separate rights. A different פסוק gives the right to eat, so ״כל זכר״ gives the right to a share. This is the source for the משנה's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Dividing up the portions of the קרבנות among the כהנים

steps.whatToRemember: Blemished כהנים may eat because of ״לחם אלהיו… יאכל״. They get a share in the dividing because of ״כל זכר״.

phrases.english: Rather, for the dividing of shares.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 31.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״כל זכר״ includes blemished כהנים in the dividing of shares, not in eating.

steps.title: Another ברייתא learns from ״כל זכר״ by the חטאת
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא says the words ״כל זכר״ in the section of the חטאת include blemished כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: ״Every male״ comes to include blemished כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא that uses the same words, ״כל זכר״, from a different פסוק, the one about the חטאת. It also says these words include בעלי מומין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already have one ״כל זכר״ that gives blemished כהנים a share (step 32). Now a second ״כל זכר״ also seems to teach about בעלי מומין. That sets up the question of what this extra one adds.

keyTerms.meaning: To include (to add something to the law)
כהנים who have a physical blemish

phrases.english: It is taught in another ברייתא:
"Every male" comes to include blemished kohanim.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:22, in the section about the חטאת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a second ״כל זכר״ after the first one was explained as being about the share.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ״כל זכר״ by the חטאת includes בעלי מומין.

steps.title: What does this second ״כל זכר״ add?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what this extra ״כל זכר״ is needed for, since eating and getting a share are already taught elsewhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what? If for eating, that is already said! If for getting a share, that is already said!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what this new ״כל זכר״ is for. Both easy answers are already covered by other פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating was already allowed by a separate פסוק, and getting a share was already learned from the first ״כל זכר״. So this second ״כל זכר״ must teach something new, and the גמרא wants to know what.

keyTerms.meaning: For what purpose?
That is already stated
Getting a share when the קרבנות are divided

phrases.english: For what?
If for eating, that is already stated!
If for getting a share, that is already stated!
phrases.notes: This points back to the first ״כל זכר״ from step 32.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַאי? אִי לַאֲכִילָה – הֲרֵי כְּבָר אָמוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions what the ברייתא in step 33 adds.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new law does the second ״כל זכר״ teach?

steps.title: It adds a כהן born with a מום
steps.stepSummary: The second ״כל זכר״ teaches that a כהן who had a מום from birth also gets a share, not only one who became blemished later.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because I might have thought I only know about a כהן who was whole and then became blemished. From where do I know about one blemished from birth? The פסוק says: ״Every male.״
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers that we might have thought only a כהן who was once whole keeps his share. This ״כל זכר״ teaches that even a כהן born with a מום gets one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן who was once fit had a time of full status, so we might have said only he keeps his rights. The extra ״כל זכר״ shows that a מום from birth does not take away the share either.

keyTerms.meaning: Whole, without a blemish
From the start (here: from birth)
The פסוק teaches (says)

phrases.english: Because one might have thought: I have only
one who was whole and then became blemished;
from where do I know one blemished from birth?
The verse says: "Every male."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 34.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The second ״כל זכר״ includes a כהן who was blemished from birth.

steps.title: A third ברייתא learns from ״כל זכר״ by the אשם
steps.stepSummary: Yet another ברייתא says ״כל זכר״, this time in the section of the אשם, includes a blemished כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: ״Every male״ comes to include a blemished כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third ברייתא with the same words ״כל זכר״, from the פסוק about the אשם. It also includes a בעל מום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there is a third ״כל זכר״. Eating, the share, and a מום from birth are all already covered, so this one must teach something new again.

keyTerms.meaning: Guilt offering

phrases.english: It is taught in another ברייתא:
"Every male" comes to include a blemished kohen.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:6, in the section about the אשם.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a third ״כל זכר״ after the second was explained.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ״כל זכר״ by the אשם includes a בעל מום.

steps.title: What does the third ״כל זכר״ add?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks again what this ״כל זכר״ is for, since eating, the share, and a מום from birth are all already taught.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what? If for eating, that is already said! And if for getting a share, that is already said! And if for one blemished from birth, that is already said!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same question as before, now with three options already used up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each earlier ״כל זכר״ already taught one point. So the גמרא crosses out all three and needs a fourth new point for this פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Eating (the meat of the קרבן)

phrases.english: For what?
If for eating, that is already stated!
And if for getting a share, that is already stated!

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי לְבַעַל מוּם מֵעִיקָּרוֹ – הֲרֵי כְּבָר אָמוּר!
phrases.english: And if for one blemished from birth, that is already stated!
phrases.notes: That was the answer of the previous ברייתא, in step 35.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַאי? אִי לַאֲכִילָה – הֲרֵי כְּבָר אָמוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions what the ברייתא in step 36 adds.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new law does the third ״כל זכר״ teach?

steps.title: It adds a כהן with a temporary מום
steps.stepSummary: The third ״כל זכר״ teaches that a כהן with a passing, temporary מום also gets a share, not only one with a permanent מום.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because I might have thought I only know about a כהן with a permanent מום. From where do I know about one with a temporary מום? The פסוק says: ״Every male.״
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers that this ״כל זכר״ adds a כהן whose מום will go away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא assumes the permanent מום is the obvious case and the temporary מום needs an extra פסוק. That order is about to be questioned.

keyTerms.meaning: A permanent blemish
A temporary blemish that will go away

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the order: the ברייתא treats the permanent מום as the simple case and the temporary one as the new חידוש. The next step asks why it isn't the other way around.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁיָּכוֹל אֵין לִי אֶלָּא בַּעַל מוּם קָבוּעַ,
phrases.english: Because one might have thought: I have only one with a permanent blemish;
from where do I know one with a temporary blemish?
The verse says: "Every male."

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁיָּכוֹל אֵין לִי אֶלָּא בַּעַל מוּם קָבוּעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 37.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The third ״כל זכר״ includes a כהן with a מום עובר.

steps.title: Isn't that backwards?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the ברייתא's order seems upside down.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't it the other way around?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא: it seems backwards to call the temporary מום the harder case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A permanent מום seems more serious than a temporary one. So we would expect the temporary מום to be the obvious case and the permanent one to need the extra פסוק. The ברייתא says the opposite.

keyTerms.meaning: Which way is it going? Isn't it the opposite?

phrases.english: Isn't it the opposite?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the order of the answer in step 38.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that a מום קבוע is obvious and a מום עובר needs a פסוק.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A permanent מום is more serious, so it should be the case that needs the extra פסוק, not the temporary one.

steps.title: רב ששת: flip the wording
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת answers by reversing the ברייתא's two cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: Reverse it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת fixes the problem by switching the order. The ברייתא should say the temporary מום is obvious and the permanent מום needs ״כל זכר״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the order is flipped, the ברייתא fits the logic of step 39. The extra פסוק now teaches the more surprising case, the permanent מום.

keyTerms.meaning: Reverse, switch the order

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said: Reverse it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 39 by changing the ברייתא's wording.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the order of the text
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא as written treats the מום עובר as the new point.
steps.terutzMaskana: Switch it: the מום קבוע is the new point taught by ״כל זכר״.

steps.title: רב אשי: keep the wording and explain it
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the ברייתא does not need to be flipped and starts to explain why the temporary מום needed a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Really, do not reverse it. It was needed, because it might have entered your mind to say:
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי keeps the ברייתא as it is. This line is a setup: he begins to explain what we might have wrongly thought, and the explanation continues in the next part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי disagrees with רב ששת and keeps the original order. He will show a reason why a temporary מום could be treated worse, so a פסוק was needed to include it.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, in fact (keeping the original view)
It was needed
It might have entered your mind to say

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Really, do not reverse it;
and it was needed, because it might have entered your mind to say:

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: לְעוֹלָם לָא תֵּיפוֹךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to step 39's קשיא and rejects רב ששת's reversal.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Keeping the text and explaining the logic
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We would have thought a מום עובר does not get a share.
steps.terutzMaskana: So ״כל זכר״ was needed to include the מום עובר; the reason continues in the next part.
